Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): Generic summation: from the pathwise per-step inequality eta A_t <= F_t - F_{t+1} + c + kappa Er_t (kappa >= 0, eta > 0), integrability and E Er_t <= e_t, conclude (1/T) sum_{t<T} E A_t <= E[F_0 - F_T]/(T eta) + c/eta + (kappa/eta)(1/T) sum e_t on a probability space. True: integrate, telescope, divide by T eta. This is the 'summing over t' step of lines 640-641 / 700-701.

Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): If 18^4 r K Delta sigma^2/eps^4 + 18^2 K Delta/eps^2 + 18^2 r^2 sigma^4/(K Delta eps^2) <= T (r, K, Delta, T, eps > 0) then 6((r K Delta sigma^2/T)^{1/4} + sqrt(K Delta/T) + r sigma^2/sqrt(K Delta T)) <= eps. True: each of the three terms is <= eps/18. With K = L_* it is Theorem 4.3's horizon; with K = r L it gives Theorem 4.1's thresholds 18^4 r^2 L Delta sigma^2, 18^2 r L Delta, 18^2 r sigma^4/(L Delta).

Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): With W_{t+1} = W_t - eta orthogonalize(M_t), eta >= 0: ||W_t - W_0||_F <= t eta sqrt r and ||W_t - W_0||_op <= t eta. True (||U V^T||_F <= sqrt r, ||U V^T||_op <= 1). Used to bound the iterates for integrability of f(W_t) and ||grad f(W_t)||_*.

Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): For the Algorithm 1 trajectory (W_t = (trajectory t).2.1, samples i.i.d. under P with marginal mu) under Assumption 3.1 (differentiable, L-Lipschitz Frobenius gradient, L >= 0), Assumption 3.3 (IsStochasticGradient with sigma >= 0), f bounded below, eta > 0, 0 <= beta < 1, B, T >= 1: every W_t is measurable, ||grad f(W_t)||_* and f(W_t) are integrable, and (1/T) sum_{t<T} E||grad f(W_t)||_* <= E[f(W_0) - f(W_T)]/(T eta) + L r eta/2 + 2 sigma sqrt(r(1-beta))/sqrt(B(1+beta)) + 2 beta sigma sqrt r/((1-beta) T sqrt B) + 2 r eta beta L/(1-beta). Exactly the Theorem 4.1 first display (line 260) with all source constants; true (per-step DDESC bound, E||M_t - C_t||_F <= (sigma/sqrt B)(sqrt a + beta^{t+1}), drift sqrt r beta L eta/(1-beta), summed with geom_tail_le; verified in graph review). Integrability holds since the iterates stay within distance T eta sqrt r of W_0 and f, grad f are continuous.
Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): sum_{t<T} beta^{t+1} <= beta/(1-beta) for 0 <= beta < 1: true.
Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): A measurable real function bounded in absolute value by a constant is integrable on a probability space: true.

Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): gradient f is measurable for every f : Mat m n -> R. True: Mathlib's measurable_fderiv holds for arbitrary f on finite-dimensional spaces, and gradient = toDual.symm o fderiv.

Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): Lemma A.3 for the Algorithm 1 trajectory: with C_0 = grad f(W_0), C_{t+1} = beta C_t + (1-beta) grad f(W_{t+1}) and M_t = (trajectory (t+1)).2.2 (the momentum produced at iteration t), under Assumption 3.3 + i.i.d. sampling, sigma >= 0, 0 <= beta < 1, B >= 1: ||C_t - M_t||_F is integrable and E||C_t - M_t||_F <= sqrt((1-beta)/(1+beta)) sigma/sqrt B + beta^t sigma/sqrt B, for every t >= 0. Exactly the statement of Lemma A.3 (line 567); no smoothness needed (as accepted). True: momentum_noise gives the second-moment bound and Jensen plus sqrt(x+y) <= sqrt x + sqrt y (or noise_mean_bound, since beta^{t+1} <= beta^t).

Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): If X is measurable with E||X||^2 <= (sigma^2/B)(a + (1-a) beta^{2t}), a = (1-beta)/(1+beta), sigma >= 0, B >= 1, then ||X|| is integrable and E||X|| <= (sigma/sqrt B)(sqrt a + beta^{t+1}). True: Jensen gives sqrt of the second moment; momentum_sqrt_le with y = beta^t (accepted stoch unit) gives the bound. This is the refined per-t noise bound whose sum gives the source's beta/(1-beta) coefficient.
Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): x >= 0 and x^4 = Q imply Q^(1/4) = x (real rpow): true.
Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): Triangle inequality for the operator norm: true.
Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): ||0||_op = 0: true.

Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): Same for Assumption 3.2 (nuclear/operator Lipschitz gradient, constant L >= 0): conclusion is the Theorem 4.3 first display (line 291): L eta/2, 2 sigma sqrt(r(1-beta))/sqrt((1+beta)B), 2 beta sigma sqrt r/((1-beta) T sqrt B), 2 eta beta L/(1-beta). True by the spectral per-step bound, ||.||_* <= sqrt r ||.||_F on the noise, and drift beta L eta/(1-beta).

Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): Generic tuned algebra (B = 1): with K > 0, r > 0, sigma >= 0, 0 <= beta < 1, T > 0, eta > 0, eta = sqrt((1-beta) Delta/(T K)), 1 - beta = (if sigma = 0 then 1 else min(sqrt(K Delta)/(sigma sqrt(r T)), 1)), E <= Delta: E/(T eta) + K eta/2 + 2 sigma sqrt(r(1-beta))/sqrt(1+beta) + 2 beta sigma sqrt r/((1-beta)T) + 2 eta beta K/(1-beta) <= 6((r K Delta sigma^2/T)^{1/4} + sqrt(K Delta/T) + r sigma^2/sqrt(K Delta T)). True: Delta > 0 is forced by eta > 0; with q = 1 - beta, the left side is <= X + Y/2 + 2 sigma sqrt(r q) + 2 sigma sqrt r/(q T) + 2X where X = sqrt(K Delta/(q T)); if q < 1 this is 5X + Y/2 + 2Z with X = (r K Delta sigma^2/T)^{1/4}, Z = r sigma^2/sqrt(K Delta T); if q = 1 it is <= 3.5 Y. With K = L_* it is Theorem 4.3's tuned claim; with K = r L it is exactly Theorem 4.1's (eta = sqrt((1-beta)Delta/(r T L)), 1 - beta = min(sqrt(L Delta)/(sigma sqrt T), 1), rate terms (r^2 L Delta sigma^2/T)^{1/4}, sqrt(r L Delta/T), sqrt r sigma^2/sqrt(L Delta T)), so one lemma serves both.

Statement (registered sorry body, not evidence): sum_{i<t+2} w^{(t+1)}_i N_i = beta sum_{i<t+1} w^{(t)}_i N_i + (1-beta) N_{t+1} with w^{(t)}_0 = beta^t, w^{(t)}_i = (1-beta) beta^{t-i} (i >= 1): the closed form M_t = (1-beta) sum_{i=1}^t beta^{t-i} G_i + beta^t G_0 of line 585 satisfies the momentum recursion.
